'''Nododo''' was the [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Deity/Legends|god]] of trickery in the [[Gungan religion|religion]] of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. He was considered one of the less serious [[Gud/Legends|guds]] in the pantheon who would choose to provide entertainment in spite of his divine nature. Other such guds included [[Kobble]], the goddess of good [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] and feasting, and [[Wamka Pol]], the god of games. Nododo had the power to change his appearance, taking the form of animals to visit and insult Gungans.<ref name="SWGB" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|This was a bit of extreme referencing, extrapolated from the Lucas Learning children's game ''Yoda's Challenge'' where one of the puzzles revolved around the player recovering some sacred statues from a series of catacombs. The statues were in the shape of an opee sea killer, a kaadu, a peko peko, and a shaak, which seemed to fit well into the already-established tenets of Gungan pantheism.|Daniel Wallace, explaining information about Nododo written for the canceled reference book ''The Essential Guide to Episode I''|<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|34|Lostwords: The Essential Guide to Episode I}}</ref>}}
Nododo was originally created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], written by [[George Lucas]]. In the film's revised rough draft, the Gungan [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] attempts to convince his companion, the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], that their impending journey through Naboo's core will lead to their [[Death/Legends|deaths]]. Kenobi retorts that his access to the power of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] will protect them, but Binks responds in disbelief that reliance on the Force is comparable to praying to Nododo.<ref name="Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> The scene where Nododo was mentioned did not appear in the finished film,<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> which premiered on [[May 19]], [[1999]],<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> although it was described in the CD-ROM ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide]]'',<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> which was released on [[June 23]], 1999.<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news19990623.html|text=''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''Insider's Guide''}}</ref> Nododo was then established to exist [[canon]]ically within the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity when he was mentioned in the [[Wikipedia:French language|French language]] version of the Gungan DataBank in the [[2001]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''.<ref name="SWGB" />

[[File:Nododo_statues.png|thumb|right|300px|The animal statues in ''Yoda's Challenge Activity Center'' that were going to be retroactively linked to Nododo by ''The Essential Guide to Episode I'']]
Author [[Daniel Wallace]] planned to elaborate on Nododo's nature in the ultimately canceled reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Episode I]]''. In a blog post on [[StarWars.com]] that explored the content intended for the book, Wallace stated that Nododo would have been identified as a trickster god who could only appear as an [[Opee sea killer/Legends|opee sea killer]], a [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]], a [[Peko-peko/Legends|peko peko]], or a [[Shaak/Legends|shaak]]. Nododo's forms were intended to reference a puzzle from<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|34|Lostwords: The Essential Guide to Episode I}}</ref> the [[Lucas Learning]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]'',<ref name="Yoda">''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]''</ref> which was released on [[August 11]], 1999.<ref name="Release date">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news19990806.html|text=Are You Ready For Yoda's Challenge?}}</ref> In the game's "Explore the [[Gungan Caves]]" activity, the player had to recover [[Unidentified Gungan sacred statues|sacred statues]] that bore the shapes of the aforementioned species from a series of catacombs. Wallace believed that the statues fit well into existing details about the Gungan religious beliefs.<ref name="Blog" />
